articles.summary: Futures margin requirements function as a performance bond, not a loan, covering potential losses on leveraged contracts. This guide explains initial, maintenance, and intraday margin types, how exchanges like CME Group set and adjust requirements, and how to trade futures on Webull with a minimum $100 account equity.
articles.title: Futures Margin Requirements: A Complete Guide for US Traders

articles.summary: Futures tick value is the dollar amount of a contract's minimum price move, calculated as tick size multiplied by the point value (contract multiplier). This guide covers tick value definitions, reference tables for equity index, energy, metals, currency, and crypto futures, step-by-step P&L formulas, risk management techniques, and how to trade futures on Webull.
articles.title: Futures Tick Value: Complete Guide to Calculation, Contract Specs, and Risk Management

articles.summary: A futures contract rollover means closing a near-expiring front-month position and reopening equivalent exposure in the next active contract. This guide covers rollover timing by market, roll yield in contango and backwardation, chart gap artifacts, open interest signals, and a step-by-step process for rolling futures positions on Webull.
articles.title: Futures Contract Rollover: A Trader's Complete Guide
